hooks.text: Most people think a tsunami destroys everything it touches.
How did a Navy warship end up as a desert inn?
A massive wave hit Arica, but it didn't sink this ship.

title: Why was a Navy Ship in the Arica Desert? 🤯
description: In 1868, a massive tsunami in Arica carried the USS Wateree inland, leaving it perfectly upright in the Atacama desert.

beats.text: Most people think a tsunami destroys everything it touches.
beats.visual: Engraving of a massive tsunami wave striking a coastal city, 19th century

beats.text: In 1868, a massive earthquake leveled the port of Arica, Peru.
beats.visual: Ruins of buildings in Arica after the 1868 earthquake

beats.text: While other ships were crushed, the USS Wateree had a flat bottom.
beats.visual: Illustration of the USS Wateree sidewheel gunboat at sea

beats.text: The massive wave carried the gunboat inland without tipping it over.
beats.visual: Illustration of a massive tsunami wave lifting ships in a harbor

beats.text: It sat perfectly upright, five hundred yards into the desert.
beats.visual: Historic photograph of the USS Wateree sitting upright in the desert
